Aug 20, 2014 9:22:43 GMT -5 sunbelle said:
Hi Mike,
We are experience something very similar with many of our leucos as well. Pitchers are up early, but it seems like some of the plants (like our Purple Lip x self clone 2)are going back to producing phyllodia. This particular plant produced a flurry of pitchers a couple of weeks ago and then stopped, and its sibling is now sending up big traps. Other leucos are sending up pitchers too. This is early for us, and we are in the middle of the "mean season" down here in south Florida--nights are upper seventies and days are mid nineties. Usually the leucos are resting, and don't start with pitchers until late Sept.-Oct.
We are south of their habitat where conditions are more tropical, and we're experiencing something similar to you, living north of their typical habitats. We've talked to other growers living in the "Sarracenia Belt" who are having this occur too.
Go figure...



Thanks for sharing your observations Sunbelle, that's really fascinating! I always thought the leucos under warmer temperatures would start producing their fall pitchers much earlier, but it almost sounds like the heat wave holds them off temporarily.

Calen: very surprised to hear you're already getting large fall pitchers, that's great to hear! A few days ago, I wasn't so sure if my plants would produce fall pitchers, but now I can see that "adult pitcher primordia" pushing out from the growth point, so there will definitely be a nice show in a few weeks. Stay tuned, I have a couple of new clones that haven't been photo-documented yet, including some neat pure leucos from the wilkerson's bog.

posts.body_html:
The fall traps on S. leucophylla var. alba clone A Baldwin Co, AL look profoundly different from spring and summer traps! to make things even more interesting, this clone ages like fine wine: it starts off like a regular leucophylla, but as the traps age, they color up and get whiter and whiter, and eventually it becomes an alba! Can these traps start off as albas right when they open? Probably, but under the conditions here, this is how they "act." Pics taken 9/27/20:


The lines in the interior of the mouth are slowly fading away as the traps age:




This clone is very similar to S. leucophylla var. alba 'white back' Baldwin Co, AL ( sarracenia.proboards.com/thread/4295/leucophylla-alba-white-back-baldwin ) in the sense that the back of the trap can get very white, but when they just open up, they're not necessarily very white. I'm not sure if the back of the trap on this one will get solid white this year,we'll see!
